newsitem.title: USA: EPA calls for better labels on pet pesticides.
newsitem.headline: EPA calls for better labels on pet pesticides.

text.p: The Environmental Protection Agency said Friday it was requiring better labels on pesticides for cats and dogs to make sure they are used more safely.
The new rules call for clearer directions on products such as flea and tick dips, sprays, powders and collars.
Labels should include statements like: "Do not use (on dogs or cats) under 12 weeks," and "Consult a veterinarian before using this product on debilitated, aged, pregnant or nursing animals."
The EPA said improved directions were necessary because vets, pet owners and manufacturers of pet pesticides had reported harmful effects from the products.
